title: Where can I find the sample map of the dlc I bought?

posts.author: WhereAmI74
posts.body:
I'm a beginner in RPG maker.
When I buy a tileset officially purchased on Steam or various websites, it is sometimes difficult to set the passage one by one.
Because just the tileset PNG file comes without passage
I wish I could get the same sample map as the sample map image on the store page
Is there a way to i get it?
mainly in the case of purchase from steam.
I wonder, Can I get the purchase receipt I received by email if I send it to the producer or distributor and ask them to send me a sample map?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
first, a sample map wouldn't help you at all, because the maps do not contain tileset definitions.
you would need a tileset file or similar information.
second, a lot of DLC don't have either sample map or sample tile definitions, they have only sample pictures for the shop.
There are ways to store and load tileset definitions, but unfortunately they are rarely used at all.
Because most people like to tweak the tileset definitions to their own games - and clicking through tile definitions might be tedious but is done much more quickly than developing an entire game.
If you give a name of a specific tileset someone can check if there is such a definition file, but the chance is very low.

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
Has the artist(s) who created the tile set a website or Discord server? If they have, it is possible that there might be something there for you to download. Earlier this year I bought some Winlu tile sets, and later was told about the example maps downloadable from their Discord server.
It might be worth you asking about the particular tiles that you bought in case anyone has any relevant information.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Andar said:
first, a sample map wouldn't help you at all, because the maps do not contain tileset definitions.
you would need a tileset file or similar information.
Click to expand...
That's not really accurate. I've never purchased a tileset that came with a demo project/sample maps where the tileset passability wasn't defined in the database.
Andar said:
second, a lot of DLC don't have either sample map or sample tile definitions, they have only sample pictures for the shop.
Click to expand...
That is true, not all tilesets come with demo projects.
Andar said:
There are ways to store and load tileset definitions, but unfortunately they are rarely used at all.
Click to expand...
This is not at all necessary in order to have passability - you can simply copy and paste the tileset's database entry from one project to another and it will copy all passability settings. The tileset definition file is only to show the name of the tile when mousing over it in the editor.
WhereAmI74 said:
When I buy a tileset officially purchased on Steam or various websites, it is sometimes difficult to set the passage one by one. Because just the tileset PNG file comes without passage
I wish I could get the same sample map as the sample map image on the store page
Is there a way to i get it?
Click to expand...
As Andar said, you need to see whether the description of the product says it comes with a demo project. If not, you just need to figure it out yourself - making a video game by yourself is going to involve a lot of tedious work.
WhereAmI74 said:
I wonder, Can I get the purchase receipt I received by email if I send it to the producer or distributor and ask them to send me a sample map?
Click to expand...
No. You can try, but I can't imagine anyone would do that for you.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
ATT_Turan said:
The tileset definition file is only to show the name of the tile when mousing over it in the editor.
Click to expand...
I wasn't talking about the text file at all, I was talking about a plugin/tool created by shaz (iirc) that reads and stores the tileset info from the database, and can then load the stored file to create the database definition again.
It was supposed to be used with every later shop tileset exactly to help with this setup but unfortunately that plan fell apart.
